chapterTitle: Faith That Overcomes and the Certainty of Eternal Life
themeTitle: “That You May Know That You Have Eternal Life”

scripture.text: Whoever believes that Jesus is the Christ has been born of God. Whoever loves the Father also loves the child who is born of him.
scripture.understanding: πᾶς ὁ πιστεύων ὅτι Ἰησοῦς ἐστιν ὁ Χριστός, “Whoever believes that Jesus is the Christ” — the test of truth; the man Jesus is the Messiah, the Son of God. ἐκ τοῦ θεοῦ γεγέννηται, “has been born of God” — γεννάω, from the birth family, perfect tense: faith is the evidence of a birth that has already happened. καὶ πᾶς ὁ ἀγαπῶν τὸν γεννήσαντα ἀγαπᾷ καὶ τὸν γεγεννημένον ἐξ αὐτοῦ, “Whoever loves the Father also loves the child who is born of him” — ἀγαπάω, from the love family; γεννάω three times in one verse. Love the Father, love His family.

scripture.text: By this we know that we love the children of God, when we love God and keep his commandments.
scripture.understanding: ἐν τούτῳ γινώσκομεν ὅτι ἀγαπῶμεν τὰ τέκνα τοῦ θεοῦ, “By this we know that we love the children of God” — γινώσκω, from the know family; ἀγαπάω, from the love family; τέκνον, from the children family. ὅταν τὸν θεὸν ἀγαπῶμεν καὶ τὰς ἐντολὰς αὐτοῦ τηρῶμεν, “when we love God and keep his commandments” — τηρέω, from the hold family (many manuscripts read ποιῶμεν, ‘do’). Love for God's children is proved by loving God and obeying Him, not by sentiment alone.

scripture.text: For this is loving God, that we keep his commandments. His commandments are not grievous.
scripture.understanding: αὕτη γάρ ἐστιν ἡ ἀγάπη τοῦ θεοῦ, ἵνα τὰς ἐντολὰς αὐτοῦ τηρῶμεν, “For this is loving God, that we keep his commandments” — ἀγάπη, from the love family; τηρέω, from the hold family. Love is not only feeling but obedience. καὶ αἱ ἐντολαὶ αὐτοῦ βαρεῖαι οὐκ εἰσίν, “His commandments are not grievous” — βαρύς, heavy, crushing: Jesus said, ‘my yoke is easy, and my burden is light’ (Matthew 11:30). The new nature delights in what it once resented.

scripture.text: For whatever is born of God overcomes the world. This is the victory that has overcome the world: your faith.
scripture.understanding: ὅτι πᾶν τὸ γεγεννημένον ἐκ τοῦ θεοῦ νικᾷ τὸν κόσμον, “For whatever is born of God overcomes the world” — γεννάω, from the birth family; νικάω, to conquer; κόσμος, from the world family: the whole system that opposes God. καὶ αὕτη ἐστὶν ἡ νίκη ἡ νικήσασα τὸν κόσμον, ἡ πίστις ἡμῶν, “This is the victory that has overcome the world: your faith” — νίκη, victory, the only time this noun appears in the New Testament; πίστις, faith. Faith unites us to Christ, who has overcome the world (John 16:33).

scripture.text: Who is he who overcomes the world, but he who believes that Jesus is the Son of God?
scripture.understanding: τίς ἐστιν ὁ νικῶν τὸν κόσμον, “Who is he who overcomes the world” — νικάω; κόσμος, from the world family. εἰ μὴ ὁ πιστεύων ὅτι Ἰησοῦς ἐστιν ὁ υἱὸς τοῦ θεοῦ, “but he who believes that Jesus is the Son of God?” — not self-discipline, not knowledge, but faith in the person of Jesus.

scripture.text: This is he who came by water and blood, Jesus Christ; not with the water only, but with the water and the blood. It is the Spirit who testifies, because the Spirit is the truth.
scripture.understanding: οὗτός ἐστιν ὁ ἐλθὼν δι᾽ ὕδατος καὶ αἵματος, “This is he who came by water and blood, Jesus Christ” — the strongest reading is that ‘water’ refers to His baptism, where He was declared the Son, and ‘blood’ to His death on the cross. οὐκ ἐν τῷ ὕδατι μόνον, ἀλλ᾽ ἐν τῷ ὕδατι καὶ ἐν τῷ αἵματι, “not with the water only, but with the water and the blood” — against teachers who said the divine Christ came on Jesus at baptism but left before the cross. The Son of God really died. καὶ τὸ πνεῦμά ἐστιν τὸ μαρτυροῦν, ὅτι τὸ πνεῦμά ἐστιν ἡ ἀλήθεια, “It is the Spirit who testifies, because the Spirit is the truth” — μαρτυρέω, to bear witness.

scripture.text: For there are three who testify:
scripture.understanding: ὅτι τρεῖς εἰσιν οἱ μαρτυροῦντες, “For there are three who testify” — μαρτυρέω. The Law required two or three witnesses (Deuteronomy 19:15). Some later Bibles, following a few late Latin and Greek manuscripts, add here ‘in heaven: the Father, the Word, and the Holy Spirit; and these three are one’; this addition is not found in any Greek manuscript before the fourteenth century, and the WEB rightly omits it. The Trinity is taught throughout Scripture without it.

scripture.text: the Spirit, the water, and the blood; and the three agree as one.
scripture.understanding: τὸ πνεῦμα καὶ τὸ ὕδωρ καὶ τὸ αἷμα, “the Spirit, the water, and the blood” — three witnesses to Jesus: the Spirit (at His baptism and in believers), the water (His baptism) and the blood (His cross). John also saw blood and water flow from Jesus' side (John 19:34). καὶ οἱ τρεῖς εἰς τὸ ἕν εἰσιν, “and the three agree as one” — they give one united testimony.

scripture.text: If we receive the witness of men, the witness of God is greater; for this is God’s testimony which he has testified concerning his Son.
scripture.understanding: εἰ τὴν μαρτυρίαν τῶν ἀνθρώπων λαμβάνομεν, “If we receive the witness of men” — μαρτυρία, testimony: we accept human testimony every day in courts and in life. ἡ μαρτυρία τοῦ θεοῦ μείζων ἐστίν, “the witness of God is greater” — μείζων, greater. ὅτι αὕτη ἐστὶν ἡ μαρτυρία τοῦ θεοῦ ὅτι μεμαρτύρηκεν περὶ τοῦ υἱοῦ αὐτοῦ, “for this is God’s testimony which he has testified concerning his Son” — μαρτυρέω, perfect tense: God's witness stands.

scripture.text: He who believes in the Son of God has the testimony in himself. He who doesn’t believe God has made him a liar, because he has not believed in the testimony that God has given concerning his Son.
scripture.understanding: ὁ πιστεύων εἰς τὸν υἱὸν τοῦ θεοῦ ἔχει τὴν μαρτυρίαν ἐν ἑαυτῷ, “He who believes in the Son of God has the testimony in himself” — the external witness becomes an inner conviction by the Spirit. ὁ μὴ πιστεύων τῷ θεῷ ψεύστην πεποίηκεν αὐτόν, “He who doesn’t believe God has made him a liar” — unbelief is not neutral; it calls God a liar. ὅτι οὐ πεπίστευκεν εἰς τὴν μαρτυρίαν ἣν μεμαρτύρηκεν ὁ θεὸς περὶ τοῦ υἱοῦ αὐτοῦ, “because he has not believed in the testimony that God has given concerning his Son.”

scripture.text: The testimony is this, that God gave to us eternal life, and this life is in his Son.
scripture.understanding: καὶ αὕτη ἐστὶν ἡ μαρτυρία, “The testimony is this” — μαρτυρία. ὅτι ζωὴν αἰώνιον ἔδωκεν ἡμῖν ὁ θεός, “that God gave to us eternal life” — ζωή, from the life family: the life of God Himself; αἰώνιος, from the time family; δίδωμι, a gift. καὶ αὕτη ἡ ζωὴ ἐν τῷ υἱῷ αὐτοῦ ἐστιν, “and this life is in his Son” — eternal life is not a thing apart from Christ; it is found only in Him.

scripture.text: He who has the Son has the life. He who doesn’t have God’s Son doesn’t have the life.
scripture.understanding: ὁ ἔχων τὸν υἱὸν ἔχει τὴν ζωήν, “He who has the Son has the life” — ζωή, from the life family. ὁ μὴ ἔχων τὸν υἱὸν τοῦ θεοῦ τὴν ζωὴν οὐκ ἔχει, “He who doesn’t have God’s Son doesn’t have the life.” — the dividing line is not religion, knowledge or morality, but whether you have the Son.

scripture.text: These things I have written to you who believe in the name of the Son of God, that you may know that you have eternal life, and that you may continue to believe in the name of the Son of God.
scripture.understanding: ταῦτα ἔγραψα ὑμῖν, “These things I have written to you” — the purpose of the whole letter. τοῖς πιστεύουσιν εἰς τὸ ὄνομα τοῦ υἱοῦ τοῦ θεοῦ, “who believe in the name of the Son of God” — written to believers. ἵνα εἰδῆτε ὅτι ζωὴν ἔχετε αἰώνιον, “that you may know that you have eternal life” — οἶδα, from the know family and the see family: settled knowledge, not hopeful guessing; ζωή, from the life family; αἰώνιος, from the time family; present tense: you have it now. His Gospel was written that people might believe (John 20:31); his letter that believers might know.

scripture.text: This is the boldness which we have toward him, that, if we ask anything according to his will, he listens to us.
scripture.understanding: καὶ αὕτη ἐστὶν ἡ παρρησία ἣν ἔχομεν πρὸς αὐτόν, “This is the boldness which we have toward him” — παρρησία, the confidence of 3:21, now in prayer. ὅτι ἐάν τι αἰτώμεθα κατὰ τὸ θέλημα αὐτοῦ ἀκούει ἡμῶν, “that, if we ask anything according to his will, he listens to us” — αἰτέω, from the pray family; θέλημα, His will; ἀκούω, to hear with favour. Prayer is not bending God's will to ours, but bringing ours to His (Matthew 26:39).

scripture.text: And if we know that he listens to us, whatever we ask, we know that we have the petitions which we have asked of him.
scripture.understanding: καὶ ἐὰν οἴδαμεν ὅτι ἀκούει ἡμῶν, “And if we know that he listens to us” — οἶδα, from the know family (and the see family). ὃ ἐὰν αἰτώμεθα, οἴδαμεν ὅτι ἔχομεν τὰ αἰτήματα ἃ ᾐτήκαμεν ἀπ᾽ αὐτοῦ, “whatever we ask, we know that we have the petitions which we have asked of him” — αἰτέω and αἴτημα, both from the pray family: the asking and the thing asked. The answer is as good as received when we ask according to His will.

scripture.text: If anyone sees his brother sinning a sin not leading to death, he shall ask, and God will give him life for those who sin not leading to death. There is a sin leading to death. I don’t say that he should make a request concerning this.
scripture.understanding: ἐάν τις ἴδῃ τὸν ἀδελφὸν αὐτοῦ ἁμαρτάνοντα ἁμαρτίαν μὴ πρὸς θάνατον, “If anyone sees his brother sinning a sin not leading to death” — εἴδω, from the see family (and the know family); ἁμαρτάνω and ἁμαρτία, from the sin family. αἰτήσει, “he shall ask” — αἰτέω, from the pray family. καὶ δώσει αὐτῷ ζωήν, “and God will give him life” — ζωή, from the life family. ἔστιν ἁμαρτία πρὸς θάνατον, “There is a sin leading to death.” οὐ περὶ ἐκείνης λέγω ἵνα ἐρωτήσῃ, “I don’t say that he should make a request concerning this” — ἐρωτάω, a second word from the pray family: to make a request, as distinct from αἰτέω. The strongest reading in context is that the ‘sin leading to death’ is the deliberate, persistent rejection of Christ shown by the antichrists who left the church (2:19, 22); others connect it with the sin against the Spirit (Matthew 12:31) or with sins God judges by physical death (1 Corinthians 11:30). John does not forbid praying, but does not command it in that case.

scripture.text: All unrighteousness is sin, and there is a sin not leading to death.
scripture.understanding: πᾶσα ἀδικία ἁμαρτία ἐστίν, “All unrighteousness is sin” — two words from the sin family: ἀδικία, wrongdoing, injustice, and ἁμαρτία, missing the mark. Every wrong is serious. καὶ ἔστιν ἁμαρτία οὐ πρὸς θάνατον, “and there is a sin not leading to death” — most sins of believers, confessed and forgiven (1:9).

scripture.text: We know that whoever is born of God doesn’t sin, but he who was born of God keeps himself, and the evil one doesn’t touch him.
scripture.understanding: οἴδαμεν ὅτι πᾶς ὁ γεγεννημένος ἐκ τοῦ θεοῦ οὐχ ἁμαρτάνει, “We know that whoever is born of God doesn’t sin” — οἶδα, from the know family (and the see family); γεννάω, from the birth family; ἁμαρτάνω, from the sin family, present tense: does not keep on sinning as a way of life (3:9). ἀλλ᾽ ὁ γεννηθεὶς ἐκ τοῦ θεοῦ τηρεῖ ἑαυτόν, “but he who was born of God keeps himself” — τηρέω, from the hold family. The WEB follows manuscripts reading ‘himself’; many early manuscripts read ‘him’, which would make ‘he who was born of God’ Jesus Himself, the eternal Son, who keeps the believer (John 17:12). καὶ ὁ πονηρὸς οὐχ ἅπτεται αὐτοῦ, “and the evil one doesn’t touch him” — πονηρός, from the evil family; ἅπτομαι, to lay hold of, to grab.

scripture.text: We know that we are of God, and the whole world lies in the power of the evil one.
scripture.understanding: οἴδαμεν ὅτι ἐκ τοῦ θεοῦ ἐσμεν, “We know that we are of God” — οἶδα, from the know family (and the see family). καὶ ὁ κόσμος ὅλος ἐν τῷ πονηρῷ κεῖται, “and the whole world lies in the power of the evil one” — κόσμος, from the world family; πονηρός, from the evil family; κεῖμαι, to lie, as a child lies in someone's arms: the world is held in the evil one's grip. There are two families and two realms.

scripture.text: We know that the Son of God has come, and has given us an understanding, that we know him who is true, and we are in him who is true, in his Son Jesus Christ. This is the true God, and eternal life.
scripture.understanding: οἴδαμεν δὲ ὅτι ὁ υἱὸς τοῦ θεοῦ ἥκει, “We know that the Son of God has come” — οἶδα, from the know family (and the see family); ἥκω, to have come and to be present. καὶ δέδωκεν ἡμῖν διάνοιαν ἵνα γινώσκωμεν τὸν ἀληθινόν, “and has given us an understanding, that we know him who is true” — διάνοια, the mind, the capacity to understand; γινώσκω, also from the know family; ἀληθινός, genuine, real, as opposed to false gods. οὗτός ἐστιν ὁ ἀληθινὸς θεὸς καὶ ζωὴ αἰώνιος, “This is the true God, and eternal life” — the strongest reading takes ‘this’ as Jesus Christ, the nearest name: Jesus is the true God and eternal life. ζωή, from the life family; αἰώνιος, from the time family.

scripture.text: Little children, keep yourselves from idols.
scripture.understanding: τεκνία, φυλάξατε ἑαυτὰ ἀπὸ τῶν εἰδώλων, “Little children, keep yourselves from idols” — τεκνίον, from the children family; φυλάσσω, from the hold family: to guard, as a sentry guards a post, as distinct from τηρέω in verse 18. εἴδωλον, an idol: in Ephesus, the temple of Artemis; in John's letter, also every false idea of God that replaces ‘the true God’ of verse 20. The letter ends with a warning that guards everything it has taught.

visualMeditations.title: The Victory of Faith
visualMeditations.image: Picture a besieged city, surrounded by enemy armies. Inside, the people are weak and outnumbered. But the gates open, and their King rides out alone — and the enemy scatters. The people inside did not win by their own strength; they won because they belonged to the King who conquered.
visualMeditations.meaning: “For whatever is born of God overcomes the world. This is the victory that has overcome the world: your faith” (v. 4). “Who is he who overcomes the world, but he who believes that Jesus is the Son of God?” (v. 5). Faith is not a weapon you swing harder; it is the bond that unites you to the One who has already overcome the world.

visualMeditations.title: Water and Blood
visualMeditations.image: Picture a river in Judea where a crowd watches a man come up from the water as the heavens open and a voice speaks. Then picture a hill outside Jerusalem three years later, where a soldier drives a spear into the side of the same man, and blood and water flow out.
visualMeditations.meaning: “This is he who came by water and blood, Jesus Christ; not with the water only, but with the water and the blood” (v. 6). His baptism declared Him the Son; His death proved He truly came in the flesh and truly died for sin. The Spirit, the water and the blood agree: this is the Son of God.

visualMeditations.title: The Certificate of Life
visualMeditations.image: Picture someone who has been adopted holding an official certificate with their name, signed by a judge and sealed. They no longer wonder whether they belong. When doubts come, they take out the document and read it again: it is settled.
visualMeditations.meaning: “The testimony is this, that God gave to us eternal life, and this life is in his Son” (v. 11). “He who has the Son has the life” (v. 12). “These things I have written to you who believe in the name of the Son of God, that you may know that you have eternal life” (v. 13). God's word is your certificate. If you have the Son, you have the life.

visualMeditations.title: Guarding the Gate
visualMeditations.image: Picture a temple in Ephesus, its huge statue of Artemis surrounded by crowds and incense. Then picture a small house nearby where a handful of believers gather, and an old man says to them, ‘Little children, keep yourselves from idols.’ At the door of the house a watchman stands, keeping guard through the night.
visualMeditations.meaning: “We know that we are of God, and the whole world lies in the power of the evil one” (v. 19). “We know that the Son of God has come, and has given us an understanding, that we know him who is true” (v. 20). “Little children, keep yourselves from idols” (v. 21). Having found the true God, guard your heart against every substitute.

structure.label: Faith, Love and Obedience Together (v. 1-5)
structure.body: Everyone who believes that Jesus is the Christ is born of God, and whoever loves the Father loves His children; we know we love God's children when we love God and obey Him, and His commands are not burdensome; everyone born of God overcomes the world through faith that Jesus is the Son of God.

structure.label: The Testimony About the Son (v. 6-12)
structure.body: Jesus Christ came by water and blood, and the Spirit testifies; the Spirit, the water and the blood agree; God's testimony is greater than human testimony; whoever believes has the testimony within, whoever does not makes God a liar; the testimony is that God has given eternal life in His Son: whoever has the Son has life.

structure.label: Assurance and Prayer (v. 13-17)
structure.body: John writes so that believers may know they have eternal life; we have confidence that God hears us when we ask according to His will, and we know we have what we ask; pray for a brother committing sin not leading to death, and God will give him life; there is sin leading to death, and all wrongdoing is sin.

structure.label: Three Certainties and a Final Warning (v. 18-21)
structure.body: We know that the one born of God does not keep on sinning and the evil one cannot touch him; we know we are from God while the whole world lies in the evil one's power; we know the Son of God has come and given us understanding to know the true God, and He is the true God and eternal life; little children, guard yourselves from idols.

sections.heading: Faith That Overcomes
paragraphs: Chapter 5 ties together the three tests of the letter. Truth: “Whoever believes that Jesus is the Christ has been born of God” (v. 1). Love: “Whoever loves the Father also loves the child who is born of him” (v. 1). Obedience: “For this is loving God, that we keep his commandments. His commandments are not grievous” (v. 3). These are not three separate checklists but three expressions of one new birth. And the commands are not heavy, because a new nature loves what God loves. Jesus said, “For my yoke is easy, and my burden is light” (Matthew 11:30).

The result is victory: “For whatever is born of God overcomes the world. This is the victory that has overcome the world: your faith” (v. 4). The ‘world’ here is the whole system of pride, desire and unbelief that John has described (2:15–17). Believers overcome it not by withdrawing from it or by sheer willpower, but by faith that unites them to Christ, who said, “In the world you have oppression; but cheer up! I have overcome the world” (John 16:33).

And that faith has a specific object: “Who is he who overcomes the world, but he who believes that Jesus is the Son of God?” (v. 5). Not faith in faith, or in ourselves, or in a vague higher power, but faith in Jesus as the Son of God. The person of Christ is always at the centre of John's letter.

sections.heading: Water, Blood and the Testimony of God
paragraphs: Verse 6 is one of the more difficult verses: “This is he who came by water and blood, Jesus Christ; not with the water only, but with the water and the blood.” The strongest reading is that ‘water’ means Jesus' baptism, where the Spirit descended and the Father declared Him the Son (Mark 1:10–11), and ‘blood’ means His death. Some false teachers apparently said that the divine Christ came upon the man Jesus at His baptism but left Him before the cross, so that only a man died. John says no: the Son of God came through both the water and the blood. The One who was baptised is the One who died.

John then speaks of three witnesses: “the Spirit, the water, and the blood; and the three agree as one” (v. 8). Some older English Bibles add words here about ‘the Father, the Word, and the Holy Spirit’ in heaven. That addition does not appear in any Greek manuscript before the fourteenth century and was not part of what John wrote, so modern translations, including the WEB, rightly leave it out. The doctrine of the Trinity rests securely on the whole of Scripture without it.

Then John argues from the lesser to the greater: “If we receive the witness of men, the witness of God is greater” (v. 9). And God's testimony is simple: “The testimony is this, that God gave to us eternal life, and this life is in his Son” (v. 11). “He who has the Son has the life. He who doesn’t have God’s Son doesn’t have the life” (v. 12). Eternal life is not earned, discovered or achieved; it is a gift found only in Christ. To refuse to believe this is to call God a liar (v. 10).

sections.heading: That You May Know
paragraphs: Now John states the purpose of the whole letter: “These things I have written to you who believe in the name of the Son of God, that you may know that you have eternal life” (v. 13). The false teachers had shaken the church's confidence. John has given tests — truth, obedience and love — not to make believers anxious but to make them sure. His Gospel was written “that you may believe that Jesus is the Christ, the Son of God, and that believing you may have life in his name” (John 20:31); his letter is written so that those who believe may know.

That assurance gives confidence in prayer: “This is the boldness which we have toward him, that, if we ask anything according to his will, he listens to us” (v. 14). Prayer according to God's will is not a weakness of faith but its heart, as Jesus prayed, “nevertheless, not what I desire, but what you desire” (Matthew 26:39).

Verses 16–17 apply this to praying for others. If a believer sees a brother sinning, he should pray, and God will give life. But “There is a sin leading to death” (v. 16). Christians have understood this differently. In the context of 1 John, the strongest reading is that it refers to the deliberate, persistent denial of Christ shown by the antichrists who left the church (2:19, 22) — a rejection of the only source of life. Others link it with the sin against the Holy Spirit (Matthew 12:31) or with sins God judges by physical death (1 Corinthians 11:30). John does not forbid prayer, but he will not command it in that case. What he does command is that believers pray for each other.

sections.heading: Three Certainties and One Warning
paragraphs: John closes with three ‘we know’ statements. First: “We know that whoever is born of God doesn’t sin, but he who was born of God keeps himself, and the evil one doesn’t touch him” (v. 18). The believer does not live in sin as a way of life, and the evil one cannot seize him. Many manuscripts read ‘keeps him’, so that ‘he who was born of God’ is Jesus Himself, who keeps His people — as He prayed, “keep them from the evil one” (John 17:15).

Second: “We know that we are of God, and the whole world lies in the power of the evil one” (v. 19). There are two families and two kingdoms; believers belong to God, even while living in a world held in the enemy's grip. Third: “We know that the Son of God has come, and has given us an understanding, that we know him who is true, and we are in him who is true, in his Son Jesus Christ. This is the true God, and eternal life” (v. 20). The most natural reading is that ‘this’ refers to Jesus Christ: He is the true God and eternal life. John 17:3 says, “This is eternal life, that they should know you, the only true God, and him whom you sent, Jesus Christ.”

And then, abruptly, the last line: “Little children, keep yourselves from idols” (v. 21). After revealing the true God, John warns against every substitute — the carved idols of pagan Ephesus, and every false image of God that the false teachers offered. Anything we put in the place of the true God revealed in Jesus Christ is an idol. Paul says, “Therefore, my beloved, flee from idolatry” (1 Corinthians 10:14). The letter that began with what was seen and touched ends with a guard at the door of the heart.

ntConnection.heading: The Witness of the Father, the Victory of the Son and the Keeping of His Own
paragraphs: The water of verse 6 points to Jesus' baptism: “Immediately coming up from the water, he saw the heavens parting, and the Spirit descending on him like a dove” (Mark 1:10), and “A voice came out of the sky, ‘You are my beloved Son, in whom I am well pleased’” (Mark 1:11). John the Baptist testified, “I have seen the Spirit descending like a dove out of heaven, and it remained on him” (John 1:32). The blood points to the cross, where John watched as “one of the soldiers pierced his side with a spear, and immediately blood and water came out” (John 19:34).

God's testimony to His Son (v. 9) is a theme of John's Gospel: “The Father himself, who sent me, has testified about me” (John 5:37), and “It’s also written in your law that the testimony of two people is valid” (John 8:17). The confidence in prayer of verse 14 rests on Jesus' promise: “Whatever you will ask in my name, that will I do, that the Father may be glorified in the Son” (John 14:13).

The keeping of verse 18 echoes Jesus' prayer: “I pray not that you would take them from the world, but that you would keep them from the evil one” (John 17:15), and His promise: “I give eternal life to them. They will never perish, and no one will snatch them out of my hand” (John 10:28). The true God of verse 20 is the One revealed at the end of the Bible: “behold, a white horse, and he who sat on it is called Faithful and True” (Revelation 19:11).

lexicon.insight: Strong's: “conquest (abstractly), i.e. (figuratively) the means of success.” νίκη appears only here in the New Testament; its verb νικάω appears six times in 1 John and seventeen in Revelation. Nike was the Greek goddess of victory. John says the believer's victory is not a goddess, nor human strength, but faith — trust in Jesus as the Son of God. The dictionary's phrase is apt: faith is ‘the means of success’, because it joins us to the One who has already won.

Strong's: “evidence given (judicially or genitive case).” μαρτυρία and μαρτυρέω appear ten times in verses 6–11. It is courtroom language: evidence that establishes the truth. The witnesses are the Spirit, the water and the blood — and above all God Himself. Our word ‘martyr’ comes from it: those who bore witness to Christ with their lives. God's testimony is not a feeling but a fact: eternal life is in His Son.

lexicon.strongs: G2065 (ask αἰτέω, aitéō, G154; petitions αἴτημα, aítēma, G155)
lexicon.insight: Strong's: “to interrogate; by implication, to request.” Verses 14–16 use three words from the pray family. αἰτέω is to ask, as a child asks a father; αἴτημα is the request itself; ἐρωτάω is to ask as one making a request of an equal, or to question. John says believers should αἰτέω for a sinning brother, but does not tell them to ἐρωτάω about the sin leading to death. The variety of words shows that prayer is personal, specific and governed by God's will.

Strong's: “truthful.” ἀληθινός means genuine, real, true as opposed to fake or counterfeit — not merely ‘truthful’ in speech, but the real thing. John uses it three times in verse 20: we know Him who is true, we are in Him who is true, and Jesus Christ is the true God. In a city full of idols, and a church disturbed by false teachers, John ends by pointing to the only genuine God — and gives believers διάνοια, the understanding to recognise Him.

Strong's: “an image (i.e. for worship); by implication, a heathen god, or (plural) the worship of such.” εἴδωλον is from εἶδος, form, appearance: an image that looks like a god but is not. Ephesus, where John probably lived, was home to the vast temple of Artemis. But John's last warning reaches beyond statues to every false god — including false versions of Jesus. φυλάσσω, from the hold family, is a guard's word: stand watch over your heart.

holySpiritRevelation.intro: In this final chapter the Holy Spirit wants to settle your assurance, strengthen your prayers and guard your heart.

items.title: Do You Know?
items.body: John wrote “that you may know that you have eternal life” (v. 13). The Spirit does not want you living in constant uncertainty. If you believe that Jesus is the Son of God, love His people and want to obey Him, then you have the Son — and “He who has the Son has the life” (v. 12). Take God at His word today.

items.title: Pray for Your Brother
items.body: “If anyone sees his brother sinning a sin not leading to death, he shall ask, and God will give him life” (v. 16). The Spirit brings to mind a believer who is struggling, straying or caught in sin. Instead of criticising or gossiping, pray for them — specifically and persistently — and trust God to give life.

items.title: What Has Taken God's Place?
items.body: “Little children, keep yourselves from idols” (v. 21). An idol is anything you trust, fear, love or obey more than the true God. The Spirit asks gently: what has crept into the place that belongs to Him? Money? Approval? A relationship? Comfort? A false picture of God? Name it, and give that place back to Jesus, the true God.

audit.title: The Assurance Check
audit.body: If someone asked you today, ‘Do you know you have eternal life?’, what would you say? On what would you base your answer (vv. 11–13)?

audit.title: The Prayer Check
audit.body: Do you pray with confidence according to God's will (vv. 14–15)? Are you praying for a brother or sister who is struggling with sin (v. 16)?

audit.title: The Idol Check
audit.body: What competes with God for your trust, love and obedience (v. 21)? What false ideas of God or Jesus have you been tempted to accept?

practices.title: Write Your Assurance
practices.body: Write out verses 11–13 by hand. Underneath, write: ‘I have the Son. Therefore I have the life.’ Then list the evidences John has given in the letter that you see in your own life — faith in Jesus, desire to obey, love for believers, the Spirit's witness. Keep it where you will see it on days of doubt.

practices.title: Smash an Idol
practices.body: This week, identify one ‘idol’ in your life (v. 21). Take a practical step to dethrone it — fast from it, give it away, confess it to a trusted friend, or replace the time it takes with time in God's word and prayer. Then pray verse 20 aloud: ‘This is the true God, and eternal life.’

prayerReflection: “Father, I believe that Jesus is the Christ, the Son of God, and I thank You that I have been born of You. Let my love for You show in loving Your children and keeping Your commands, which are not a burden to me. Thank You that the victory that overcomes the world is faith in Your Son. Thank You for the testimony of the Spirit, the water and the blood, and for Your own testimony: that You have given me eternal life, and that this life is in Your Son. I have the Son, so I have the life. Let me know it with settled confidence. Give me boldness in prayer, to ask according to Your will, knowing that You hear me. Help me pray faithfully for my brothers and sisters who stumble. Thank You that the One born of You keeps me, and the evil one cannot touch me. Thank You that the Son of God has come and given me understanding to know You, the true God. Jesus, You are the true God and eternal life. Guard my heart from every idol. In Your name, Amen.”

storyConnections.title: The Baptism of Jesus
storyConnections.summary: Jesus came from Nazareth to be baptised by John in the Jordan. As He came up out of the water, He saw the heavens torn open and the Spirit descending on Him like a dove, and a voice came from heaven: “You are my beloved Son, in whom I am well pleased” (Mark 1:11). John the Baptist testified, “I have seen the Spirit descending like a dove out of heaven, and it remained on him” (John 1:32). The water of His baptism, the Spirit's descent and the Father's voice all bore witness to who He was — the ‘water’ of 1 John 5:6.

storyConnections.title: Blood and Water at the Cross
storyConnections.summary: After Jesus died, the soldiers came to break the legs of the crucified men to hasten their deaths. Finding Jesus already dead, they did not break His legs, but “one of the soldiers pierced his side with a spear, and immediately blood and water came out” (John 19:34). John adds that the one who saw it has testified so that you may believe. He was that eyewitness. The real blood of a real death is the ‘blood’ of 1 John 5:6 — proof that the Son of God truly came in the flesh and truly died for sin.

storyConnections.title: Paul and the Silversmiths of Ephesus
storyConnections.summary: In Ephesus, Paul's preaching turned so many people from idols that the silversmiths who made shrines of Artemis lost business. Their leader, Demetrius, stirred up a riot, and the whole city rushed into the theatre shouting for two hours, ‘Great is Artemis of the Ephesians!’ Many years later John lived in the same city, among the same temples. His last line to the churches of Asia — ‘Little children, keep yourselves from idols’ — was not abstract. The true God had come in Jesus Christ; every other god, however great its temple, was a lie.
